rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines clear verses as unambiguous and firmly binding, like a rope that restrains the soul from wandering and directs it toward beneficial ends.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهي التي أبرم حكمها فلم ينبتر كما يبرم الحبل الذي يتخيذ حكمة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: He treats the clear verses as enduring ordinances of worship whose rulings remained unchanged across the three revealed books.
rows.anchor: فهي آي التعبد من الخلق للخلق اللائي لم يتغير حكمهن في كتاب من هذه الكتب الثلاث المذكورة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The clear verses form the comprehensive source toward which other meanings return; the Mother is an origin from which spiritual things are derived and bodily things grow.
rows.anchor: وقال الحرالي : هي الأصل المقتبس منه الشيء في الروحانيات والنابت منه أوفيه في الجسمانيات

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: He defines ambiguity as outward resemblance between two matters that hides the distinctive features of each.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : والتشابه تراد التشبه في ظاهر أمرين لشبه كل واحد منهما بالآخر بحيث يخفي خصوص كل واحد منهما

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The ambiguous verses concern divine self-disclosure and acts, which creatures cannot fully grasp; clear verses guide practice, while ambiguous ones establish faith through recognition of human incapacity, and the books differ in four legal categories.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : والتشابه تراد التشبه في ظاهر أمرين لشبه كل واحد منهما بالآخر بحيث يخفي خصوص كل واحد منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God divides revelation into clear and ambiguous passages as a test, as He also creates extraordinary cases such as Jesus born without a male seed, to distinguish the firmly grounded from others.
rows.anchor: فبين سبحانه وتعالى بهذا أنه كما يفعل الأفعال المتشابهه مثل تصوير عيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام من غير نطفة ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The firmly grounded believe all revelation is from God and seek His help to unlock difficult passages by returning them to the clear; the author's example is Christians who took Jesus' ambiguous sayings literally.
rows.anchor: يستـنصرون منه سبكانه وتعالى فتح المنغلق وبيان المشكل حتى يفتحه عليهم بما يرده إلى المحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic passages cited present Jesus as God's servant and prophet who calls God his Lord, and say that he taught worship of God alone.
rows.anchor: إني عبد الله آتني الكتاب وجعلني نبيا وجعلني مباركا أين ما كنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if Christians altered their scriptures, the four Gospels available to the author contain enough clear statements to interpret their ambiguous passages.
rows.anchor: ففي إنجيل لوقا أن جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام ملاك الرب لما تبدى لمريم مبشرا بالمسيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luke's annunciation has Gabriel tell Mary she will bear Jesus, who will be great and receive the throne of David his father.
rows.anchor: ويعطيه الرب كرسي داود أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus answers Satan's temptations by citing the command not to test the Lord and to worship the Lord alone, and the Gospels state that God is one.
rows.anchor: مكتوب : لا تجرب الرب إلهك , وقال وقد أمره أن يسجد له : مكتوب : للرب إلهك اسجد , وإياه وحده اعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luke depicts Jesus reading Isaiah's prophecy that the Spirit of the Lord is upon him because God anointed and sent him to preach.
rows.anchor: روح الرب علي , من أجل هذا مسحني وأرسلني لأبشر المساكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Gospels say that receiving or hearing Jesus means receiving or hearing the one who sent him, and that denying Jesus also denies his sender.
rows.anchor: من قبل هذا فقد قبلني , ومن قبلني فقد قبل الذي أرسلني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: John portrays Jesus as sent by God, speaking God's words, doing the sender's will, and judging only by what he hears rather than acting independently.
rows.anchor: لست أقدر أعمل شيئا من ذات نفسي , وإنما أحكم بما أسمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mark's sayings distinguish God's commands from human traditions and record Jesus rebuking a follower for thinking about human rather than divine concerns.
rows.anchor: اذهب يا شيطان ! فإنك لم تفكر في ذات الله , وتفكر في ذات الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Gospels show Jesus praying to God and teaching disciples to pray, and identify the temple as a house of prayer.
rows.anchor: يا رب ! علمنا نصلي كما علم يوحنا تلاميذه , فقال لهم : إذا صليتم فقولوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' title Lord reflects God's permission for him to perform extraordinary acts; Lord can also mean master, as in Joseph's request to be remembered by his master.
rows.anchor: والرب يطلق على السيد أيضا , كما قال يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the opening of John's Gospel interprets Lord as knowledge.
rows.anchor: ثم وجدت في أوائل إنجيل يوحنا أن الرب تأويله العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Father and son language can mean that God nurtures, protects, aids, honors, and magnifies Jesus as a father does his child, rather than biological parentage.
rows.anchor: أن الله سبحانه وتعالى يفعل معه ما يفعل الوالد مع ولده من الترية والحياطة والنصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' teachings call believers God's children when they imitate divine mercy, give charity secretly, and pray privately, showing that Father is figurative language for care and honor.
rows.anchor: لكيما تكونوا بني أبيكم الذي في السماوات , لأنه المشرق شمسه على الأخبار والأشرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Jesus says his mother and brothers are those who hear and practice God's word, Christians should likewise read his family language figuratively.
rows.anchor: أمي وأخواتي الذين يسمعون كلمة الله ويعملون بها ؛ فكذلك يلزمهم تأويلها في حق عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking divine fatherhood literally for Jesus while reading it figuratively for believers is inconsistent, since every person has human parents; the author says Jesus himself supplied evidence for a figurative reading.
rows.anchor: فإن كل أحد منهم مساو لجميع الناس وللبهائم في أن له أبوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus calls himself Son of Man to state his real human nature; language assigning him to God is metaphorical.
rows.anchor: ابن الإنسان يفعل كذا , ابن البشر قال كذا يعني نفسه الكريمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah permits prostration to people as reverence, but Islamic law forbids prostration to anyone but God and forbids calling God Father or Son or using terms implying deficiency.
rows.anchor: وأما نحن فلا يجوز فعله لغير الله , ولا يجوز في شريعتنا أصلا إطلاق الأب ولا الابن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims interpret divine pleasure, anger, mercy, laughter, hand, palm, and eye by their fitting implications, denying bodily likeness while affirming God's perfection.
rows.anchor: حملنا ذلك كله على أن المراد منه لوازمه وغاياته مما يليق بجلاله سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Ambiguous revelation lets God become known through what resembles creatures, reveals their lower rank, and completes their knowledge by teaching them the limit of their understanding and their incapacity.
rows.anchor: وجه إنزال هذا الحرف تعرف الحق للخلق بمعتبر ما خلقهم عليه ليفتوا عنه وليفهموا خطابه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Reflection on the ordered heavens reveals no flaw, while repeated looking returns the eye humbled and exhausted; this illustrates human limits before divine matters.
rows.anchor: فارجع البصر هل ترى من فطور

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: God teaches humans about themselves and others after their birth in ignorance, then makes them unable to know His affair, past and future days, or the unseen present.
rows.anchor: أعلمهم بحظ من علم أنفسهم وغيرهم بعد أن أخرجهم من بطون أمهاتهم لا يعلمون شيئا ثم أعجزهم عن علم أمره

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Humans can submit voluntarily and gain certainty about God's command and unseen days, just as they submitted by necessity in infancy; God grants them a share of knowledge about creation.
rows.anchor: ليسلموا له اختيار فيرزقهم اليقين بأمره وغائب أيامه , كما أسلموا له في الصغر اضطرارا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Trying to grasp ambiguous divine speech through proof, thought, or interpretation forfeits certainty and distracts people from clear duties, like watching a king instead of observing his rules.
rows.anchor: وحاول تدركه بدليل أو فكر أو تأويل حرم اليقين بعلي الأمر والتحقيق في علم الخلق

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The first rank of ambiguity is known only by God's direct disclosure, without thought or inference; the disjoined letters at the starts of twenty-nine surahs train creatures to stop and surrender, as in the opening of al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: جامع الحروف المنزلة في أوائل السور التسع والعشرين من سوره وبه افتتح الترتيب في القرآن

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The second rank is detailed ambiguous discourse about God's self-disclosure, acts, creation, wisdom, unseen dominion, might, and the states of His days.
rows.anchor: وأما الرتبة الثانية فمتشابه الخطاب المفصل المشتمل على إخبار الله عن نفسه وتنزيلات أمره

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali lists divine descriptions and actions across the Qur'an, including God's creating people in wombs, knowing secrets, possessing dominion, and descriptions of His face, hands, sight, and presence.
rows.anchor: هو الذي يصوركم في الأرحام

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The list continues with descriptions of divine blessing, hands, sovereignty, presence, ascent, vision, will, and coming, treating these as detailed ambiguous reports about God.
rows.anchor: إن الله وملائكته يصلون علىالنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophetic reports describe descent, feet, image, laughter, hand, and fingertips, among other matters; al-Daraqutni collected many, while theologians wrote some to interpret them and hadith authorities strongly condemned this.
rows.anchor: حديث النزول والقدمين والصورة والضحك والكف والأنامل

rows.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
rows.claim: Ahmad says the attribute verses and reports are locked chests whose keys belong to God, and their interpretation is their recitation.
rows.anchor: آيات الصفات وأحاديث الصفات صناديق مقفلة مفاتيحها بيد الله سبحانه وتعالى , تأويلها تلاوتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the Companions and Arabic-speaking community understood these reports as intended to communicate meaning, not to impart exhaustive knowledge.
rows.anchor: اجتمعت عليه الصحابة رضوان الله تعالى عليهم ولقنته العرب كلها أن ورود ذلك عن الله ومن رسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Companions were not troubled by these reports and welcomed them; one reportedly said that a Lord who laughs would never leave them without good.
rows.anchor: لا نعدم الخير من رب يضحك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars either stop at the boundary of faith, content with the communicated meaning, or receive deeper certainty; God teaches through signs in creation and tests the elite through attributes beyond full comprehension.
rows.anchor: إما متوقف عنه في حد الإيمان , قانع بما أفاد من الإفهام , وإما مفتوح عليه بما هو في صفاء الإيقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an denies any likeness to God, and the author says this opens the way to the clear certainty granted to those God loves.
rows.anchor: ليس كمثله شيء

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says faith in ambiguous revelation completes Islam because it reports God's names and attributes, which creatures cannot perceive or comprehend and must not imagine as resembling created things.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن تحقيق الإسلام بقراءة حرف المحكم لا يتم إلا بكمال الإيمان بقراءة حرف المتشابه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Inwardly, readers should know that they cannot know God's attributes and stop interpreting them out of reverence; in their state, they should humble themselves and avoid claiming attributes proper to the Lord.
rows.anchor: المعرفة بأن جميع أسماء الحق وأوصافه تعجز عن معرفتها إدراكات الخلق وتوقف عن تأويلها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Humans must recognize their poverty rather than claim divine richness, their weakness rather than God's might, and renounce the attributes of dominion, anger, pleasure, promise, and threat for themselves.
rows.anchor: لتحقق فقر الخلق من تسمي الحق بالغنى , ولا يتسمى بالغنى فيقدح في هداه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The practical reading of ambiguous revelation keeps the tongue from likeness and comparison; this counters anthropomorphism and prepares pure worship, with no other outward action required here.
rows.anchor: وليس لعمل الجوارح في هذا الحرف مظهر سوى ما ذكر من لفظ اللسان

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Those led astray by ambiguous passages have crooked hearts; al-Harali glosses deviation as a turn toward what the self finds attractive and links it to inner and behavioral lapses.
rows.anchor: وقال الحرالي : هو ميل المائل إلى ما يزين لنفسه الميل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form of 'they follow' implies persistent, effortful pursuit; an isolated slip that does not become repeated following escapes this rebuke when followed by repentance.
rows.anchor: في إشعار هذه الصيغة بما تنبئ عنه من تكلف المتابعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ambiguous material includes divine descriptions such as knowing and wisdom or anger and pleasure, as well as eye, hand, foot, and face language grounded in creaturely forms.
rows.anchor: نحو أوصاف النفس كالتعليم والحكيم وسائر أزواج الأوصاف كالغضب والرضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reveals such passages to make Himself known through familiar created forms while testing whether people restrain speculation and worship: they act on clear verses and stop before ambiguous ones.
rows.anchor: ففائدة إنزاله عملا في المحكم وفائدة إنزاله فيه توقفا عنه ليقع الابتلاء بالوجهين
